quarterly_data.quarter: Skeleton Technologies press release: Skeleton Technologies secures strategic investment led by (10-14-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Strategic investor Siemens: Skeleton announced a strategic investment from Siemens (CEO Taavi Madiberk: a '9-digit investment round led by Siemens') that will primarily accelerate the expansion of its US manufacturing footprint and R&D in Silicon Valley to meet growing demand from hyperscalers for AI data-center power systems. The release ties it to a new partnership focused primarily on AI data-center infrastructure and US hyperscaler demand: the companies will combine Siemens' industrial electrical infrastructure with Skeleton's fast-response power systems to develop and commercialize products for next-generation AI data centers, from the grid to the rack. It deepens a long-standing relationship: Siemens supported Skeleton's expansion in 2023, and Siemens Digital Industries designed and automated Skeleton's Leipzig SuperFactory in Germany.
quarterly_data.counterparty_role: strategic investor and development partner (AI data-center power products)

quarterly_data.quarter: Skeleton Technologies press release: Skeleton Technologies secures strategic investment led by (10-14-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Skeleton plans to invest more than $200 million in operational scale-up and R&D in Silicon Valley, working directly with hyperscalers; the US expansion includes plans to establish domestic cell manufacturing, creating a fully integrated US value chain from cells to complete systems (CEO Taavi Madiberk claims it would make Skeleton the only player in its segment with a full US value chain).

quarterly_data.quarter: Skeleton Technologies press release: Skeleton Technologies secures strategic investment led by (10-14-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CEO Taavi Madiberk: 'AI is scaling faster than the power infrastructure behind it. The constraint is not how many GPUs you can buy, but how much compute you can extract from every GPU and every megawatt available'; 'In AI infrastructure, supercapacitors are becoming the new semiconductors.' The company says its high-power systems - Curved Graphene cells combined with power electronics and system-level controls - eliminate harmonics and manage the rapid power swings of GPU clusters close to the workload, delivering up to 40% energy savings and double-digit improvements in GPU performance (company claims).
quarterly_data.figure: up to 40% energy savings; double-digit GPU performance improvement (company claims)
